Working notes — ticket routing

Task: assign incoming tickets to a desk. Options: A = standard queue, B = priority desk, C = regional office.

Observed tickets: refunds, shipments, and claims; north/south/east regions; small/large sizes; senders from Field Sales, Client Services, Partner Accounts, Regional Ops, Finance Desk.

Results:
- Option C was selected for REQ-2400, 2401, 2402, 2403, 2405, 2406, 2407, 2408, 2409. All rejected as not valid.
- Option B was selected for REQ-2404 (large refund, north region, Client Services, “came in through the regional office”). Rejected as not valid.
- Option A has not yet been tried.

Conclusion:
- Do not choose C for these routing requests; it has failed repeatedly across types, regions, sizes, and senders.
- Do not assume B is correct for large north-region refunds from Client Services; that exact case rejected B.
- A (standard queue) is the only untested option and is the best default for similar tickets until evidence shows otherwise.

Next actions:
- Try A for new routing tickets unless fresh evidence supports B.
- Record any successful routing choice to refine rules.
- Ignore region/size/request-type/sender as reliable cues for choosing C; none made C valid in the observed set.

Working notes — ticket routing

Task: assign tickets to A standard queue, B priority desk, C regional office.

Evidence:
- C rejected for REQ-2400–2403, 2405–2409 across types, regions, sizes, senders. Avoid C.
- B rejected for REQ-2404 (large refund, north, Client Services, “came through regional office”). No valid B yet.
- A now tested. Accepted: REQ-2411 (small refund, south, Field Sales), REQ-2412 (small refund, south, Regional Ops), REQ-2413 (small refund, south, Regional Ops; message mentions regional office). Rejected: REQ-2410 (small invoice, east, Field Sales), 2414 (small refund, south, Client Services), 2415 (small claim, north, Regional Ops), 2416 (small claim, north, Finance Desk), 2417 (small shipment, south, Field Sales), 2418 (large invoice, east, Field Sales), 2419 (small claim, south, Regional Ops).

Rule so far: A is valid for small refunds originating in south when sender is Field Sales or Regional Ops. Not valid for same type/region from Client Services. A failed for invoices, claims, shipments; east/north; large invoice. “Came through regional office” does not make C/B valid and did not block A when sender/type/region matched.

Conclusion: Prefer A for small south refunds from Field Sales or Regional Ops. Otherwise no reliable valid option; do not default to A blindly. Avoid C; B remains unproven.

Next: try A on matching small south refunds; log outcomes. For all other tickets, gather more evidence; consider B only if fresh success. Track request type, region, sender.

Working notes — ticket routing

Task: assign tickets to A standard queue, B priority desk, C regional office.

Evidence:
- C rejected broadly (REQ-2400–2409). Avoid C.
- A: valid for small refunds, south, sender Field Sales or Regional Ops (REQ-2411–2413). Invalid for small invoice east Field Sales; small refund south Client Services; small/large claims north; small shipments south/east; large invoice east. Rule unchanged.
- B: now proven. Accepted: REQ-2421 large claim, north, Regional Ops; REQ-2426 large shipment, north, Partner Accounts. Rejected: REQ-2404 large refund north Client Services; REQ-2420 large refund north Regional Ops; REQ-2423 large refund south Finance Desk. So B valid for large claim or shipment from north, at least Regional Ops/Partner Accounts; not for refunds.
- D attempts all rejected; not useful.
- “Came through regional office” does not validate C/B and does not block A when A criteria match.

Conclusion:
Prefer A for small south refunds from Field Sales or Regional Ops.
Prefer B for large north claims/shipments from Regional Ops or Partner Accounts.
Avoid C. Do not use B for refunds. Large refunds still lack a reliable valid route.

Next:
Test B on matching large north non-refund claims/shipments. Test A on matching small south refunds. For all others, gather evidence. Log request type, region, sender, size, and refund vs non-refund.

Working notes — ticket routing

Task: assign tickets to A standard, B priority, C regional.

C: avoid; broadly rejected (REQ-2400–2409).

A: valid only for small refunds, south, sender Field Sales or Regional Ops (REQ-2411–2413). Invalid for: small invoice east Field Sales; small refund south Client Services; claims north; small shipments south/east; large invoice east; small claim east Regional Ops (2431); small refund north Field Sales (2432) or Client Services (2436); small refund east Field Sales (2433); large claim south Client Services (2434). “Came through regional office” does not make C/B valid and does not make A valid when criteria fail (2432, 2436).

B: accepted for north claims/shipments, at least Regional Ops, Partner Accounts, Field Sales; size not limited (large claim 2421; large shipment 2426, 2430; small claim 2435; small shipment 2437). Also accepted large invoice east Client Services (2438). Rejected for refunds (2404, 2420, 2423) and large claim south Client Services (2439). So B: north non-refund claims/shipments; large east invoice from Client Services. Not refunds. Not south claims.

D: not useful.

Conclusion: Prefer A only for small south refunds from Field Sales/Regional Ops. Prefer B for north claims/shipments (non-refund) and large east invoice from Client Services. Avoid C. Large refunds still lack a reliable valid route.

Next: Test B on matching north claims/shipments, small north claims/shipments from other senders, and large east invoices. Test A on matching small south refunds. Log request type, region, sender, size, and refund vs non-refund.

Working notes — ticket routing

Task: assign tickets to A standard, B priority, C regional. Avoid C.

A: valid only for small refunds, south, sender Field Sales or Regional Ops (2411–2413). Invalid for all other tested cases; large refund east Partner Accounts rejected (2443). Large refunds still lack a valid route.

B valid:
- North non-refund claims, including small claim north Finance Desk (2448). Size not limiting.
- North shipments from Regional Ops, Partner Accounts, or Field Sales; not Finance Desk (2445).
- East large claims from Client Services (2440) or Partner Accounts (2446).
- Large east invoice from Client Services (2438); large east invoice from Finance Desk rejected (2447).

B invalid:
- Refunds.
- South claims (2441 small, 2442 large); south invoice (2449).
- North invoice (2444).
- Small claim east Regional Ops (2431).
- North shipment Finance Desk (2445).

“Came through regional office” does not make C/B valid, and does not rescue A when criteria fail.

Next: Test A on matching small south refunds. Test B on north claims from more senders, north shipments excluding Finance Desk, and east large claims/invoices from Client Services/Partner Accounts. Log type, region, sender, size, refund vs non-refund.

- North shipments from Regional Ops, Partner Accounts, Field Sales; not Finance Desk (2445).
- East large claims from Client Services (2440) or Partner Accounts (2446).
- Large east invoice from Client Services (2438). Invalid for large east invoice from Partner Accounts, even if “came through regional office” (2456).

- South claims (2441, 2442), south invoice (2449).
- North invoice (2444).
- Small claim east Regional Ops (2431).
- North shipment Finance Desk (2445).

D valid:
- Small north invoice Field Sales (2453).
- Small east invoice Client Services (2454).
- Small south shipment Client Services (2459).

D invalid:

“Came through regional office” does not make C/B valid, nor rescue A when criteria fail.

Test B on north claims from more senders, north shipments excluding Finance Desk, and east large claims/invoices from Client Services/Partner Accounts. Test D on non-refund invoices/shipments across regions and senders. Log type, region, sender, size, refund vs non-refund.

Working notes — ticket routing

Task: assign tickets to A standard, B priority, C regional. Avoid C. D sometimes valid for non-refunds; never for refunds.

A:
- Formerly valid for small south refunds from Field Sales/Regional Ops. Now invalid for Regional Ops small south refunds (2451, 2452) and Client Services small south refund (2469).
- Invalid for: Field Sales east small claim (2460); Regional Ops north small invoice (2463); Partner Accounts/Regional Ops/Client Services south small claims (2464, 2467 large, 2468); Regional Ops east small invoice (2466).
- Large refunds still lack valid route (2450, 2458 rejected via D).
- Treat A as rarely valid unless old untested Field Sales small south refund still applies.

B valid:
- North non-refund claims, including small claim north Finance Desk (2448). Size not limiting.
- North shipments from Regional Ops, Partner Accounts, Field Sales; not Finance Desk (2445).
- East large claims from Client Services (2440) or Partner Accounts (2446).
- Large east invoice from Client Services (2438). Invalid for large east invoice from Partner Accounts, even if “came through regional office” (2456).

B invalid:
- Refunds.
- South claims (2441, 2442), south invoice (2449).
- North invoice (2444).
- Small claim east Regional Ops (2431).
- North shipment Finance Desk (2445).

D valid:
- Small north invoice Field Sales (2453).
- Small east invoice Client Services (2454).
- Small south shipment Client Services (2459).

D invalid:
- Refunds (2450, 2455, 2458).
- Small east shipments: Regional Ops (2457), Partner Accounts (2461), Finance Desk (2462, 2465). Likely all small east shipments.

“Came through regional office” does not make C/B valid, nor rescue A when criteria fail.

Next: Test A only on Field Sales small south refunds. Test B on north claims other senders, north shipments excluding Finance Desk, east large claims/invoices from Client Services/Partner Accounts. Test D on non-refund invoices/shipments outside known invalid east small shipments. Log type, region, sender, size, refund vs non-refund.
